title: Online Evaluation: A/B Tests, Feedback and Drift
summary: Offline evals tell you whether a change is promising; real users tell you whether it works. This lesson covers running an A/B test properly, guardrail metrics, what implicit feedback can and cannot tell you, detecting drift, and the traps (like Simpson's paradox) that mislead online analysis.
objectives: Design an A/B test for an LLM feature: unit of randomisation, primary metric, sample size and duration
Analyse an A/B result with a z-test and a confidence interval for the difference, and check for sample-ratio mismatch
Define guardrail metrics and use a non-inferiority margin to decide whether a change is safe
Interpret implicit feedback and explain why explicit thumbs are a biased sample
Detect distribution drift with a population stability index and a control chart
Recognise and resolve Simpson's paradox when pooled and sliced results disagree
prerequisites: The z-test, confidence intervals and sample-size formula from [Comparing Systems You Can Trust](/learn/evaluation/comparing-systems), and slices from [Error Analysis](/learn/evaluation/error-analysis).
